framework_claims.statement: The disclosed article can be represented as a relative-signal observation, an ordinal confirmation state, and tracking-state transitions, but it cannot be parameterized from this article.
framework_claims.derivation_note: The article names a benchmark-relative signal, tier zero, a necessary upgrade condition, and cautious tracking/removal language. The benchmark, formula, thresholds, state count, and transition windows are absent.
framework_claims.scope: Descriptive reconstruction of the 2026-07-31 public article only; not a trade or forecasting specification.

framework_claims.statement: An absolute-price barrier cannot independently falsify a benchmark-relative signal unless a conversion rule or same-unit signal criterion is disclosed.
framework_claims.derivation_note: The entry observation is expressed in benchmark-relative basis points, while the stated invalidation reference is an absolute price. Both can move in opposite directions during a market-wide move.
framework_claims.scope: Evidence-quality and falsifier-consistency guardrail; it does not create a stop, target, or action rule.

framework_claims.statement: When the source reports no material signal change, its disclosed default posture is to keep observing and avoid a directional upgrade.
framework_claims.derivation_note: The conclusion and continued-tracking paragraph both map uncertainty or no change to observation rather than escalation.
framework_claims.scope: Conservative research posture only; the undefined words material, effective, and confirmed prevent mechanical replay.

framework_claims.statement: The article exposes an event-level review field set, but two source-stated removals and an open-name dashboard do not establish a calibrated exit process or performance edge.
framework_claims.derivation_note: The source reports inclusion/removal dates, reference prices, elapsed-day labels, returns, and stated reasons. The image contains only open names, and no independent fills, denominator, benchmark, probability, or calibration protocol exists.
framework_claims.scope: Method-card documentation and future hypothesis design only; no Decision, Hypothesis, or Event Memory write is authorized by this bundle.

analysis_claims.statement: The source says it tracks benchmark-relative signal-state changes; tracking inclusion/removal is not verified trade entry/exit.
analysis_claims.falsifier: Independent transaction or account evidence showing the disclosed labels are actual fills would change, but not automatically validate, the execution interpretation.

analysis_claims.statement: The signal-state and trigger vocabulary is portable only as a research hypothesis and KOL handoff, not as a score, action module, or threshold set.
analysis_claims.falsifier: A complete public formula, frozen universe, benchmark, thresholds, horizon, and point-in-time replay could support a stronger future handoff after fresh review.

analysis_claims.statement: The semantic image is an internally consistent author self-report, not independent evidence of fills, PnL, alpha, win rate, or repeatability.
analysis_claims.falsifier: Independent point-in-time holdings, fills, benchmark returns, and a complete denominator would be required before any performance interpretation changes.

analysis_claims.statement: The stated absolute-price invalidation is non-reproducible as a falsifier for the benchmark-relative signal and may only trigger refresh or manual review.
analysis_claims.falsifier: A disclosed, testable conversion from absolute price to the same benchmark-relative signal state would remove the unit-mismatch objection.
